full_judgment: 4. Defendant No. 1 and defendant No.2 contested the suit by filing two separate sets of written statements. In the written statement of defendant No.1 it was contended, inter-alia, that the superior landlords of C.S. Khatian No. 969 under tenancy Khatian No.927 along with several other khatians sold their superior interest in favour of Abdul Matin Sarkar vide registered deed No.1521 dated 20.10.1948. The suit land of C.S. Khatina No.927 was lying abandoned and the tenants were not traceable and no arrangement was made for payment of rent of the holding. Consequently the landlord entered into the land and possessed the same for more than two years in khas. Thereafter, the landlord settled the land in favour of Baser Sarder during 1359 B.S. at a jama of Rs.3/- by dhakhila. Baser Sarder possessed the land and paid rent to the landlords till the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force. During the S.A. operation the land was duly recorded in his name on the basis of the settlement. While Baser Sarder was in possession and enjoyment of the suit land, he sold 33 decimals and 52 decimals i.e. total 95 decimals land from plot No.705 vide registered deed No.3077 dated 02.05.1960 to defendant No.1 on receipt of proper consideration. After purchase defendant No.1 began to possess the suit land by paying rents to the Government mutating her name. Thus defendant No.1 has been in possession of the land for more than 30 years and the R.S. record was also prepared in her name on the basis of her physical possession in the suit land and papers and documents. Defendant No.1 sold the suit land in favour of Mizanur Rahman, Monsur Rahman, Azizur Rahman and Nurjahan Nessa by registered kabala and delivered possession thereof in their favour. The above purchasers have been possessing the suit land by mutating their names and paying rents. The unregistered exchange deed of the plaintiff was false and fabricated. Neither his predecessors nor he had any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and as such he was not entitled to any relief as prayed for.
